title: U.S. House · Georgia's 9th District
area: Northeast Georgia, including Gainesville, Dahlonega, and Toccoa.

context.text: Cook Political Report rates this race Solid Republican; Decision Desk, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball also rate it Safe/Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Andrew Clyde
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Republican primary over Sam Couvillon and Gregg Poole, 76.0%

summary.text: Andrew Clyde has represented Georgia's 9th Congressional District since 2021. He served 28 years in the U.S. Navy and founded and owns Clyde Armory, a firearms and outdoor-equipment retailer.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Navy for 28 years.
Earned a master's degree in corporate finance and entrepreneurship from the University of Georgia.
Founded and owns Clyde Armory, a firearms and military surplus retailer.
In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), sits on the House Committee on Appropriations (Subcommittees on Commerce-Justice-Science and on Labor-HHS-Education) and the House Committee on the Budget.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Appropriations and the House Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Caitlyn Gegen
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary over Nick Alex, 60.0%

summary.text: Caitlyn Gegen is a community organizer running for Georgia's 9th Congressional District. She was raised by public-school-teacher parents, is a recipient of Georgia's HOPE Scholarship, and studied at the London School of Economics.

background.text: Parents were public school teachers; describes her sister as a labor and delivery nurse in Georgia.
Received Georgia's HOPE Scholarship for college and studied at the London School of Economics, living in the United Kingdom.
Has worked as a community organizer and in local government.

priorities.text: Says she will "fight to overturn the Dobbs decision" and opposes Georgia's six-week abortion ban.
Supports "safer gun legislation," citing having grown up doing active-shooter drills in school.
Supports free tuition at public colleges and universities, citing her own experience with the HOPE Scholarship, and "free universal healthcare."

positions.summary: Wants to overturn the Dobbs decision and opposes Georgia's six-week abortion ban.
Says she will fight for "safer gun legislation."
Advocates for "free universal healthcare," saying government-provided healthcare is cheaper and produces better outcomes.
Campaign says she will work to "expand access to affordable living by increasing the minimum wage."
